query:
While Jerome was walking Cecilia through a PixInsight Ha-RGB blending workflow, someone in the chat acknowledged following the walkthrough closely but explicitly positioned themselves as outside the narrowband-PixInsight process. Who was that person?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Ruth
C. Marcus
D. Tomás
context:
[1] (about=Ruth, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:37:00) I cannot speak to the technical aspects but the image looks beautiful. Is it possible that what you have both done this evening is exactly the kind of collaboration that makes this group worth belonging to?
[2] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:32:00) Jerome I just ran the PixelMath blend on the Orion stack and I am SHAKING. The HII emission structure around the running man nebula that I have never been able to pull out is RIGHT THERE. I had completely written off narrowband blending as too technical for me and too cold-looking. This is totally different from what I imagined, the broadband colours are intact and the Ha just adds this incredible red-gold depth to the emission zones!!! I genuinely thought I hated narrowband because it looked monochromatic but you've just shown me I was wrong about the whole thing!!! 😍🌟📷
[3] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:44:00) I'm uploading the final Ha-RGB Orion to the album right now. Jerome you said the Trapezium halo was cleaner. For context everyone: three months ago I thought narrowband was a monochromatic wasteland that sucked the life out of every image. Tonight Jerome changed my entire view of what my broadband data can become. Amazeballs does not even cover it!!! 🌟🌟📷
[4] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:09:00) ok sending the FITS now. and I have to ask... I always thought narrowband looked really cold and mono, like it strips all the warmth out. is there a way to keep the broadband colour and just add the Ha detail on top? 📷
[5] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t11 @2026-07-10T20:05:00) @all I've been going back and reprocessing my Orion image from November for the hundredth time and it still looks flat compared to Jerome's work. Jerome, I know you've helped me before with the background extraction issue but I think there's something deeper I'm missing with how Ha data could work. Is there any chance you'd walk me through how you actually blend it?? 🙏📷
[6] (about=Dev, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:41:00) is that a dumb question but... if I wanted to learn PixInsight where would I even start? lowkey the walkthrough Jerome just did made more sense to me than any YouTube video I've tried
[7] (about=Tomás, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:48:00) right once the HEQ5 is running and I've got first light sorted, I want to get to the point where I can do what Cecilia just did. not there yet but that's the direction mate 🌌✨
[8] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:11:00) that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.
[9] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) the Ha-RGB blend is not complicated once you understand what you are doing, but there are three things most people get wrong that kill the result. first: your Ha data needs to be calibrated and stacked separately, not mixed in during the initial integration. second: in PixInsight you use the ChannelCombination process with Ha mapped to the red channel of a synthetic luminance, then combine with a Luminance mask to protect star colours. third, and this is where most broadband imagers fail: you need to apply a Hue-Saturation adjustment after the blend to desaturate the magenta cast that appears in the red-blue transition zones around HII regions. if you skip that step your stars look radioactive and the nebula looks like a bad Instagram filter. send me your Orion FITS stack and I will step through it with you here in the chat.
[10] (about=Jerome, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:22:00) send me the FITS file. the issue is almost certainly your background extraction in PixInsight. if you are using automatic background extractor before separating the channels you will get that muddy look. I will walk you through the correct sequence. it will take 20 minutes.
[11] (about=Cecilia, said_by=Jerome, profile, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) Jerome walked Cecilia through the Ha-RGB blend in PixInsight, and Cecilia was amazed at the result, saying she had completely written off narrowband blending as too technical and too cold-looking, but now sees it differently.
[12] (about=Cecilia, core, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) Cecilia now believes narrowband blending is not monochromatic or cold, and that it can add red-gold depth to emission zones while keeping broadband colours intact.
[13] (about=Dev, core, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) Dev wants to learn PixInsight and found Jerome's walkthrough more understandable than any YouTube video he has tried.
[14] (about=Dev, said_by=Nadia, profile, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) Nadia advised Dev to master the eyepiece before the software, saying learning to process before understanding what you are looking at produces technically sharp meaningless pictures.
[15] (about=GROUP, said_by=Harriet, group-insight, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) Harriet noted that the PixInsight walkthrough in a WhatsApp chat is a particular kind of knowledge transfer that speaks to how amateur astronomy communities work.
[16] (about=Jerome, core, t8 @2026-05-08T20:16:00) Jerome explained that the clean colour separation in his Rosette image comes from Ha-only workflow with a mono sensor, which reads every photon with equal weight, unlike a DSLR.
[17] (about=Jerome, core, t7 @2026-05-08T20:15:00) Jerome completed a 22.4-hour Ha integration of the Rosette Nebula across 9 nights with a 3nm Chroma filter, achieving SNR 47 at the faintest shell edge; uploaded to the album.
